subject: Mathematics
schema_note: Keyed by topic_id (matches maths_syllabus_jee_main.json). Same field set as the Physics NCERT-context file, with 'hard_archetypes' recalibrated to JEE-Main-level difficulty (single/dual-concept, not the multi-topic fusion typical of Advanced) and 'banned_easy_templates' generally left as a note that direct-substitution/direct-formula questions are wanted, not excluded, since that is the opposite convention from an Advanced-style file.

formulas: Number of subsets of a set with n elements = 2^n
methods: Check reflexivity, symmetry and transitivity in that order when verifying whether a relation is an equivalence relation
traps: Confusing 'into' with 'onto' functions
Forgetting to check the domain restriction when composing two functions
hard_archetypes: Given a relation defined by a condition, determine the equivalence classes it partitions the set into
Composite-function domain/range problems involving piecewise or inverse-trig functions
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct set-operation or function-classification question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Mathematical induction/reasoning-based proofs of set identities (removed as standalone units in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Modulus and argument of a complex number
Nature of roots via the discriminant
formulas: For ax²+bx+c=0: sum of roots = -b/a, product = c/a
methods: Convert a complex number to polar form (r, θ) before raising it to a power or taking roots (De Moivre-style reasoning)
traps: Choosing the wrong quadrant for the argument when a and b have mixed signs
Forgetting that complex roots of a real-coefficient quadratic always occur in conjugate pairs
hard_archetypes: Given a condition on the roots (e.g. equal in magnitude but opposite sign), form the resulting relation among coefficients
Locus problems in the Argand plane involving |z - z1| = k type conditions
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct modulus/argument calculation or roots-from-coefficients question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Formal triangle-inequality proofs and complex-number square-root extraction techniques (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Inverse of a matrix via adjoint
Consistency of a system of linear equations
formulas: For a 3-variable system: unique solution if |A|≠0; check Δ, Δ1, Δ2, Δ3 for consistency when |A|=0
Area of triangle using determinant of vertex coordinates
methods: Compute |A| first — if non-zero, the system has a unique solution and A⁻¹ exists; only check the Δx/Δy/Δz sub-determinants when |A|=0
traps: Sign errors while expanding a 3×3 determinant by cofactors
Assuming a system with |A|=0 has no solution without checking whether it has infinitely many
hard_archetypes: Given a matrix equation with an unknown parameter, find the value(s) for which the system is consistent/inconsistent
Matrix-power or matrix-satisfies-its-own-characteristic-equation (Cayley-Hamilton-style) problems
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct determinant-evaluation or matrix-inverse computation is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Elementary row/column transformation-based matrix reduction and formal properties-of-determinants proofs (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

methods: Decide whether order matters (permutation) or not (combination) before selecting the formula
traps: Double-counting arrangements when identical objects are present without dividing by the repeated-item factorial
Forgetting to subtract restricted cases (e.g. 'two people must not sit together')
hard_archetypes: Counting problems combining multiple constraints (e.g. distinct groups, some people always/never together)
Combination problems involving distribution of distinct/identical objects into groups
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct P(n,r) or C(n,r) substitution question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.

X05.chapter: Binomial Theorem and its Simple Applications
concepts: General term of a binomial expansion
formulas: For even n, middle term is T((n/2)+1); for odd n, two middle terms exist
methods: Set the exponent of the variable in the general term equal to zero to find the term independent of x
traps: Off-by-one indexing error when identifying T(r+1) vs T(r)
Forgetting there are two middle terms when n is odd
hard_archetypes: Finding a specific coefficient or ratio of coefficients across two different binomial expansions
Problems requiring the greatest term/greatest coefficient in an expansion
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct general-term or middle-term calculation is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Formal proofs of binomial-coefficient identities (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: nth term and sum of an AP/GP
Arithmetic mean and geometric mean insertion
formulas: AM ≥ GM for positive real numbers
methods: Identify whether the sequence has a constant difference (AP) or constant ratio (GP) before choosing the nth-term formula
traps: Using the AP sum formula on a GP or vice versa
Sign errors when the common ratio of a GP is negative or a fraction
hard_archetypes: Problems requiring the sum of a series that is neither pure AP nor pure GP but a combination (AP times GP terms)
AM-GM inequality-based optimisation problems
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct nth-term or sum-of-n-terms calculation is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Sums of special series (Σn², Σn³) and arithmetico-geometric progressions (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Evaluating limits (standard forms, L'Hopital-style indeterminate forms via algebraic manipulation)
Continuity and differentiability at a point
formulas: First-derivative test / second-derivative test for local maxima/minima
Equation of tangent: y - y1 = f'(x1)(x - x1)
methods: Check continuity at a point before checking differentiability there, since differentiability implies continuity but not vice versa
traps: Applying standard limit formulas without first confirming the indeterminate form (0/0 or ∞/∞)
Confusing critical points (f'(x)=0) with points of inflection
hard_archetypes: Piecewise-function continuity/differentiability problems requiring matching left-hand and right-hand derivatives at the junction point
Optimisation (maxima/minima) word problems requiring setting up the function before differentiating
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct standard-limit evaluation or basic differentiation question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Formal statement and application of Rolle's/Lagrange's Mean Value Theorems (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Standard integration techniques (substitution, by parts, partial fractions)
formulas: ∫(a to b) f(x)dx = ∫(a to b) f(a+b-x)dx (definite-integral property)
methods: Check for a definite-integral symmetry property (e.g. f(a+b-x)=f(x)) before attempting direct integration, since it often simplifies the problem substantially
traps: Forgetting the constant of integration in indefinite integrals
Sign errors when the region for area calculation dips below the x-axis
hard_archetypes: Definite integrals requiring a clever substitution or property-based simplification rather than direct evaluation
Area-between-two-curves problems requiring correct identification of intersection points and integration limits
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct standard-integral evaluation is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Integral as the limit of a Riemann sum (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Order and degree of a differential equation
Linear first-order differential equations and integrating factor
formulas: Linear DE: dy/dx + Py = Q, integrating factor IF = e^(∫P dx), solution: y·IF = ∫Q·IF dx + C
methods: Rearrange the equation into the standard linear form (dy/dx + Py = Q) before identifying P and Q and computing the integrating factor
traps: Misidentifying the order/degree when the equation contains a radical or fractional power of a derivative
Forgetting the integrating factor when the DE is linear but not directly separable
hard_archetypes: Homogeneous differential equations requiring the substitution y=vx before separating variables
Word problems (growth/decay, mixing problems) requiring formulation of the DE from a physical description before solving
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct separation-of-variables solve is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.

concepts: Straight-line forms and angle between two lines
Standard forms of parabola, ellipse and hyperbola
formulas: Parabola y²=4ax; Ellipse x²/a²+y²/b²=1; Hyperbola x²/a²-y²/b²=1
methods: Convert the given circle/conic equation to standard form by completing the square before reading off centre, radius, or other standard parameters
traps: Sign errors when converting the general circle equation to centre-radius form
Confusing the major/minor axis orientation of an ellipse (a>b vs b>a)
hard_archetypes: Locus problems combining circle/conic definitions with a moving-point condition
Common-tangent or family-of-circles problems requiring simultaneous conic-equation manipulation
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct line-equation or circle-parameter identification question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Axis translation/rotation techniques and the y=mx+c tangency-condition derivation (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Angle between two lines in space
formulas: Shortest distance between skew lines via the vector triple-product formula
methods: Normalise direction ratios into direction cosines before applying the angle-between-lines formula, to avoid magnitude-related errors
traps: Confusing direction ratios (unnormalised) with direction cosines (normalised) in formulas that require one specifically
Sign ambiguity when computing the angle between two lines (always take the acute angle)
hard_archetypes: Given two skew lines in symmetric form, compute the shortest distance between them
Problems requiring the equation of a line through a point with given direction ratios combined with an angle condition
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct direction-cosines or distance-between-two-points-in-space question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Equations of a plane, intersection of a line and a plane, and coplanarity of lines (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

concepts: Dot product and its applications (angle, projection)
Cross product and its applications (area, perpendicularity)
formulas: Area of a triangle with two given sides as vectors = (1/2)|a×b|
methods: Express all given points as position vectors from a common origin before computing a vector between two points as (position vector of head) - (position vector of tail)
traps: Confusing dot product (scalar result) with cross product (vector result) when the problem asks for area vs angle
Sign/direction errors in the cross product due to non-commutativity (a×b = -b×a)
hard_archetypes: Problems combining collinearity/coplanarity conditions with vector algebra (e.g. show three points are collinear using vectors)
Projection and component-of-a-vector-along-another-vector problems in a geometric context
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct dot-product or cross-product computation is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Scalar and vector triple product (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

methods: Construct a frequency-times-deviation table systematically before computing mean/variance for grouped data, to avoid arithmetic slips
traps: Using the population-variance formula for grouped data without the correct frequency weighting
Misapplying Baye's theorem by using P(B|A) where P(A|B) is required, or vice versa
hard_archetypes: Multi-stage conditional-probability problems (e.g. drawing without replacement across multiple stages)
Problems requiring construction and use of a full probability distribution table (mean and variance of a random variable)
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct mean/median/mode-from-a-table or basic-probability question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Bernoulli trials and binomial distribution (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)

formulas: General solution of sinθ=sinα: θ = nπ+(-1)^n α
methods: Reduce a trigonometric equation to a single trigonometric function of a single angle before applying the general-solution formula
traps: Forgetting the general solution's full family (adding 2nπ or nπ as appropriate) instead of giving only the principal value
Applying inverse-trig-function identities outside their valid domain/range
hard_archetypes: Trigonometric equations requiring a substitution (e.g. t=tan(θ/2)) to reduce to a polynomial equation
Problems requiring simplification of a sum/difference of inverse trigonometric functions to a single value
banned_easy_templates: None by difficulty. A direct identity-application or principal-value question is a legitimate, common JEE Main archetype.
out_of_scope: Heights and distances applications (removed from this unit in the 2025 rationalisation)
